title: Metroidvania - getting far with Opus and Grok
author: AdamBlue
selftext: I've been wanting to do a metroidvania, but IGAvania style, with pixel. Opus 5.5 got me pretty far, and I tested out Grok to audit and refine the main character to look pixelated. In Godot. I have built out the complete move set for the character. Now will build out the maps, progression, then take a final stab at refining the visuals. My first commercial game, Epic Space Battles, comes out Sept. 30th. [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5085480/Epic\_Space\_Battles/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5085480/Epic_Space_Battles/) which was also entirely codex and claude driving Godot.

comments.author: Crafty-Following8762
comments.body:
This looks great. It is definitely just like Castlevania… and that is far from a bad thing. It looks good. Snappy, cinematic, cool. The movement looks like it feels nice.
The visuals are a little weak — that’s all I have to criticize.

Keep us updated! I would like to see how this comes out. 

BTW I like the name because it sounds like a nod to the original Japanese name of Castlevania (Akumajō Dracula, “Demon Castle Dracula”)).

comments.author: sevenoutdb
comments.body:
I think if you wanted feedback, I would say that overall the character animation needs a little bit more fluidity, which I think you know just compared this to bloodstained or symphony of the night, etc., or dead cells. The real star for me is the death animations on your enemies. Those are really great - better than a lot of what I see in metroidvania games. Also, I would love to see a variety of weapons and different elemental effects. It’s pretty common now that you can switch between the morning star a sword, crossbow, gun spell attacks, spears, etc. and players will expect that. Also, I really can see a Belmont character there, and you might want to integrate on this archetype concept some different hero shapes and sizes. 

I also think that the backgrounds need a little work especially some of the layering and some of the foreground/background and some of the perspective work. Also, some of your brick patterns seem to repetitive and probably see if you can add some noise. 

Also, do you have any different kind of game lighting or weather effects that you could play around with? I don’t remember seeing the rain, lightning, moonlight , fire light type of effects could add some drama and visual interest. 

I checked out your other game on Steam and I think readability is really something you wanna focus on, making it clear what action you want a player to focus on and really to separate your hero and the players actions from that game the AI actions. 

I’ve been a game producer for 25 years but I haven’t done a 2D game in a long time so you could take it with a grain of salt and I totally respect that.
